summary: Repeated village displacement is expressed by II Infectum-wa, coordinated with going away and fleeing outside. Those coordinated verbs do not make hǧr causative or add a separate flight sense.
I already has a migration sense and a personal-communication example. The single II corpus occurrence supports the same broad relocation meaning, without resolving any systematic I/II distinction.

The original citation embeds a filename fragment in the translation and an old verse number; structural cleanup is tied to the exact assigned source. Source consonants are retained pending verification.
Compare inherited mḥaǧriwa with assigned mhaǧriwa and confirm the h/ḥ transcription; no silent source spelling change is proposed.
Do I hǧərle and II mhaǧarle differ in meaning or dialect, or are they parallel loan adaptations? One II example cannot decide.
